listAcquisitions.sDispositionRationale: `vaibify sessions stop` on the researcher's own host lane, which is outside the carrier's scope by design (design section 8: a trust judgement about the hub itself needs no capability). The PID comes from vaibify's own session registry and is checked for recycle-proof liveness before the signal; the signal is SIGTERM to a hub this user started.

SIGTERM to the caffeinate helper THIS process launched and holds the pid of. Not a container mutation and reachable from no request lane: it runs on claim/release and at shutdown, so a carrier admission would have nothing to admit.

Signal 0, delivering nothing -- the journal's own emptiness probe for helper and host-exec records. Callers reach it only through the probe catalog, which has already checked the recorded pid and group are usable.

Signal 0, delivering nothing -- the shared PID-existence probe behind every lock, lease and journal staleness check. PermissionError counts as alive (the process exists under another user), which is the conservative direction: it never reaps a live holder.

The router's Docker-only tail delegation: __getattr__ forwards an attribute READ to the Docker leg verbatim, raising the typed DockerLegUnavailableError when no leg exists. It mints no authority: the delegated methods are DockerConnection's own, each carrying its own admission gates, and the resource-routed surface is twelve explicit methods above it, not this fallback.

The idle self-shutdown signals os.getpid() -- this process, and only this process. The busy veto that precedes it reads dictContainerOwners so a hub can never self-retire mid-run. There is no other target reachable from this call.

Signal 0 delivers nothing: this is an existence probe, not a signal. It answers whether a recorded group still has members, which is what makes host mode's weaker quiescence claim sayable. The same fbIsUsablePid guard applies, so a zero group id can never be probed as the caller's own.

The one site that signals something vaibify did not create in this process: a host project's journaled process GROUP, on the researcher's own machine. Guarded three ways, each with a registered falsification -- the group is only ever one the host-exec journal recorded; it is signalled only while the holder pid is provably the recorded one (fbIsProcessAliveSince, recycle-proof), an unprovable identity being reported and routed to reconciliation rather than guessed at; and fbIsUsablePid refuses a zero or absent group id, which killpg would otherwise read as the CALLER's own group. Reached from POST /api/pipeline/{id}/kill under a mode-(b) carrier, and from `vaibify reconcile --terminate-recorded` on the host lane.

The host gateway's single subprocess import. Every launch goes through _ftLaunchGatedAndStream: suspended spawn behind a stdin gate, host-exec journal record promoted and identity-gated (fnPromoteJournaledHostExec) before release, admission asserted (fnAssertContainerCommandAdmitted / fnAssertDurableExecAdmitted) at the two public entry points; testHostSubprocessConfinement pins this module as the only launcher under vaibify/host/.

listRows.sExclusionRationale: A TYPED READ on the file panel's five-second poll. It supplies a path list and an operation NAME, never command text, so the adapter builds the program and the exemption cannot be handed a command. This row REPLACED a container write plus a general exec: the poll used to push its path list into /tmp because a shell argv would not hold it, which made the dashboard's timer the one thing mutating a container on a schedule -- and therefore the one thing a commit-guard carrier could not cover without holding the mutation drain on that same schedule.
listRows.sLogicalOperation: read the polled paths' modification times and the workflow's content fingerprint
listRows.sOperationMetadata: paths and one fingerprint path; no command text reaches the adapter

listRows.sLogicalOperation: ask, per plot file of one step, whether its standard PNG exists in the container

listRows.sLogicalOperation: confirm each standard PNG the conversion just wrote is present, so the route reports only what exists
listRows.sOperationMetadata: one `test -f <standard png>` per converted plot, run inside the SAME worker as the conversion so nothing can replace a standard between the write and the check

listRows.sExclusionRationale: A declared typed read, so it reaches no gated primitive and needs no admission -- which is the point: the Repositories panel polls this every five seconds, and a route on a timer that took the mutation drain would make Run Step refuse at random for as long as the panel stayed open. It replaced a shell script this module ASSEMBLED with repository names interpolated raw into echo and git -C, which was the last exec keeping GET /api/repos/{id}/status outside the commit-guard boundary.
listRows.sLogicalOperation: read branch, remote url and porcelain for every tracked repository in one typed read
listRows.sOperationMetadata: repository paths only; the git argv is fixed program text in the typed-read table, with core.fsmonitor disabled so a repository cannot choose what the poll runs

listRows.sExclusionRationale: This row IS the enforcement point, not a caller of it: admission is asserted at its two public entry points (fnAssertContainerCommandAdmitted / fnAssertDurableExecAdmitted) before it runs, and every launch is write-ahead journaled as host-exec with the child suspended behind a gate until its identity is persisted. A carrier admits callers; this is the gate they hit.

listRows.sOperationMetadata: command text in via parameter (the declared opaque-subprocess-command blind-spot row); bounded lane kills its recorded group on timeout; durable lane relies on the journaled group identity for Cancel and quiescence
